title: Insights into the temporal dynamics of identifying problem gambling on an online casino: A machine learning study on routinely collected individual account data
authors: Andersson, S.; Carlbring, P.; Lyon, K.; Bermell, M.; Lindner, P.
tldr: XGBoost trained on 35,048 Swedish online gamblers' account data reliably predicts problem gambling from behavioral features, with temporal stability confirmed across 30-, 60-, and 90-day data truncations.
problem_and_motivation: Existing methods for identifying problem gambling rely on self-report questionnaires and cross-sectional behavioral tracking, which suffer from validity issues and fail to capture temporal dynamics. Longitudinal studies that track the evolution of gambling behavior are needed but remain scarce. Predictive analytics using machine learning could offer scalable, data-driven alternatives for early identification.
approach: Player account data from a major Swedish online gambling provider covering 4.5 years (2019-2023) for n=35,048 authenticated players was used.
Feature engineering captured gambling behavior dynamics including loss chasing, betting frequency, session lengths, and spending patterns from 11 raw data frames.
Labels were derived from manual risk assessments by the gambling provider's Responsible Gambling analysts, binarized into low-risk and higher-risk categories.
Feature selection combined top 25 features identified by SHAP values and Generalized Matrix Learning Vector Quantization to optimize discriminative power.
XGBoost was trained with hyperparameter tuning via Optuna using nested forward-chaining cross-validation to preserve temporal order.
Temporal stability was evaluated by truncating each player's training data at 30, 60, and 90 days prior to their maximum timestamp.
A full year of hold-out data was reserved to evaluate real-world generalizability under simulated deployment conditions.
Bootstrap analysis of linear regression slopes assessed whether performance metrics significantly trended across decreasing amounts of historical data.
findings: num: F1 score ranged from 0.758 (full data) to 0.810 (90-day truncated) across all truncation periods.
num: ROC AUC remained stable between 0.608 and 0.621 across truncation periods.
num: Recall reached 0.984 for the 90-day truncation, indicating high sensitivity for identifying higher-risk players.
Loss chasing behavior, net balance trend, max deposit, session sum p25, and total bets daily consistently ranked as top SHAP features.
num: Bootstrap analysis found no significant performance decline for Accuracy, Recall, F1, and ROC AUC across truncations.
num: Precision showed a consistently negative slope (95% CI [-0.005, -0.001]) with increasing truncation.
Regression model accurately predicted high-risk scores (true 0.779 vs. predicted 0.722) but underestimated low-risk (true 0.557 vs. predicted 0.219).
num: Specificity was notably low, ranging from 0.036 to 0.213 across all truncation periods.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: Data pre-processing and analysis pipeline → SQL integration, feature engineering, and temporal alignment prevent data leakage.
Figure 2: Feature importance plot → Loss chasing and net balance trend dominate SHAP values across all truncations.
Figure 3: Temporal evaluation and prediction stability → Model metrics remain stable across truncation periods on hold-out set.
Figure 4: Difference between true and predicted means → Model accurately predicts high-risk but underestimates low-risk groups.
Table 1: Model performance metrics across truncations → F1 0.758-0.810, Recall 0.834-0.984, ROC AUC 0.608-0.621.
Table 2: Risk category prediction → High-risk difference 0.003-0.057, low-risk difference 0.281-0.358.

definitions.definition: Extreme Gradient Boosting, a scalable tree boosting system for classification and regression.
SHapley Additive exPlanations, a method providing consistent and locally accurate feature attribution for model predictions.
Generalized Matrix Learning Vector Quantization, a supervised learning technique that optimizes a relevance matrix to maximize class discrimination.
Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve, a threshold-independent measure of binary classification performance.
Harmonic mean of precision and recall, used to balance false positives and false negatives in classification.
An automated hyperparameter optimization framework using Bayesian methods and tree-structured Parzen estimators.
Positive Predictive Value, the proportion of true positives among all positive predictions.
Negative Predictive Value, the proportion of true negatives among all negative predictions.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This study demonstrates that machine learning predictions of problem gambling from routinely collected account data exhibit temporal stability across varying data truncation periods. The work establishes that XGBoost-based classification using behavioral features such as loss chasing and net balance trends can maintain consistent predictive performance even with reduced historical data windows. By employing a rigorous evaluation framework with nested cross-validation and temporal hold-out splits, the study provides methodological guidance for assessing prediction reliability in longitudinal behavioral data. The findings advance the field by bridging the gap between cross-sectional gambling studies and the need for temporally robust predictive models.
directly_justifies: XGBoost trained on behavioral account data achieves F1 scores of 0.758-0.810 across truncation periods.
Loss chasing behavior and net balance trend are the most influential features for predicting problem gambling.
Bootstrap analysis shows no significant performance decline for most metrics across data truncations.
Model accurately predicts high-risk scores but underestimates low-risk category.
Temporal stability of predictions supports feasibility of early detection and intervention.
Specificity remains notably low (0.036-0.213) across all truncation periods.
Data from 35,048 Swedish online gamblers over 4.5 years provides comprehensive behavioral dataset.
limits: Single gambling operator dataset may not generalize to multi-operator gambling environments.
Inconsistent application of risk labels over time may introduce temporal biases.
Imputation of unknown risk labels may introduce noise into the training data.
Limited bootstrapping approach (four samples per metric) may reduce sensitivity to trends.
Model consistently underestimates risk for the low-risk category.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. The paper is primarily relevant to domains 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles), 6 (Predictive Modeling), 8 (Anomaly Detection), 12 (Evaluation Frameworks), and 14 (ML Model Serving). Topic codes 5.A and 5.B received high relevance as the paper directly profiles gambling behavior through behavioral features and evaluates temporal profile dynamics. Topic code 6.A received high relevance for its use of XGBoost in predictive modeling. Topic code 6.B received medium relevance as it uses sequential behavioral data but is not focused on forecasting per se. Topic codes 8.A and 8.B received medium relevance since identifying problem gambling parallels anomaly detection in behavioral data. Topic codes 12.A and 12.B received medium relevance for the temporal truncation evaluation framework and rigorous model assessment methodology. Topic code 14.B received low relevance as the paper discusses real-time deployment potential but does not focus on model serving. Topic codes 1.A-3.C were rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, financial structures, or expense categorization. Topic codes 7.A-7.E were rejected as the paper does not involve budgeting strategies or recommendation. Topic codes 9.A-10.C were rejected as mobile design, offline architecture, privacy, and trust are not addressed. Topic codes 11.A-11.C were rejected as engagement and retention are not studied. Topic codes 13.A-13.C were rejected as savings and debt management are outside scope. Topic code 14.A was rejected as no synthetic data generation is involved.

limitations: Single gambling operator dataset may not generalize to multi-operator gambling environments.
Inconsistent application of risk labels over time may introduce temporal biases.
Imputation of unknown risk labels may introduce noise into the training data.
Truncation strategy may bias model toward accounts with more extensive histories.
Incomplete behavioral histories from single operator can lead to misclassification of gambling behaviors.
Limited bootstrapping approach (four samples per metric) may reduce sensitivity to subtle trends.
Model consistently underestimates risk for the low-risk category.
remember_this: XGBoost predicts problem gambling with F1 scores between 0.758 and 0.810 across truncations.
Loss chasing and net balance trend are the most predictive behavioral features.
Model predictions remain temporally stable across 30-, 60-, and 90-day data truncations.
High-risk individuals are accurately identified but low-risk individuals are consistently underestimated.
Specificity remains notably low, indicating challenges in correctly identifying non-problem gamblers.
